newsitem.title: USA: Ovid sees accounting changes affecting net.
newsitem.headline: Ovid sees accounting changes affecting net.

text.p: Ovid Technologies Inc said Tuesday that if new accounting rules about the recognition of revenue in certain software transactions are approved by the Financial Accounting Standards Board, as expected, it will report a loss in the quarter the rules are effective, though operations and cash flow will remain unaffected.
The company also said that the effect of the new rules will be seen for the following three quarters, but with diminishing impact.

Jerry McAuliffe, chief financial officer, said in a statement that Ovid expects the changes to become effective in the third quarter. He added, "Since two-thirds of our revenues are affected, the effect will be dramatic in the quarter following the change, leading to a reported loss for the quarter and will have a significant but diminishing effect for the three quarters after that.
"It should be noted, however, that this is simply a change in accounting principle and has no effect on our operating cash flows or our business fundamentals."
Ovid provides electronic information retrieval services to the biomedical, scientific and academic markets.
